about: Maloof Wines began in 2015 as the project of Bee Maloof, an aerospace materials engineer, and Ross Maloof, a veteran of Philadelphia’s restaurant wine scene, and has grown into a small team that includes Bee’s wife, Michelle McCaw. Since late 2019 they have worked from No Clos Radio, an estate vineyard and winery outside Forest Grove at the northwest edge of the Willamette Valley, first planted in the early 1970s and among the oldest surviving vineyards in the area.

Maloof is a variety-first, low-intervention producer: all of its sources are organically farmed, some dry-farmed, and the wines are fermented with native yeasts and bottled unfined and unfiltered with little or no added sulfur. Fancy Free comes from Nemarniki Vineyard, a six-acre, organic, dry-farmed site at about 800 feet in the Laurelwood District of the Chehalem Mountains, on windblown loess over volcanic basalt, best known for Maloof’s Riesling.
